 The Filter Life and style The best early UK Black Friday deals on the products we love, from heated airers to the perfect pillow
 We’ve cut through the noise to find genuinely good early Black Friday 2026 discounts on Filter-tested products across home, kitchen, fitness, beauty and more
 The best sustainable Black Friday deals 
 Jane Hoskyn Thu 19 Nov 2026 10.01 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jump to:
 The best early Black Friday deals on the Filter UK’s favourite products 
 The best home deals 
 The best food, drink and kitchen deals 
 The best personal care deals 
 The best sleep deals 
 The best fitness deals 
 The best fashion deals 
 R etailers aren’t rolling out their Black Friday discounts from the kindness of their hearts. It’s business. But if you can resist the urge to impulse-buy anything with a red ticket, and instead focus your attention on genuinely discounted items that you genuinely want, then it’s a potentially big win for you, too.
 The whole shebang lasts a fortnight these days, but it’s not quite in full swing yet. At the time of writing, the actual Friday in question (27 November) is just over a week away, and many of the best deals haven’t landed yet. Plenty of brands have been at it for days, though, with John Lewis, Boots and, inevitably, Amazon launching their Black Friday sales when you could still smell fireworks in the air.
 This is the third time we’ve rounded up Black Friday deals at the Filter, and a few items definitely seem to catch your eye year after year. A sonic toothbrush and classic Stanley flask are eternally popular, perhaps because they make good Christmas presents. At the hotter end of the price scale, a premium espresso machine , gym-quality treadmill and hybrid mattress are among your enduring Black Friday top dogs, thanks to the hundreds wiped off their prices.
 Let’s see if this year’s newcomers, from weighted blankets to heated airers , can become your new Black Friday favourites. We’ll keep this page updated as more deals appear over the next 10 days, so drop in again soon.
 How we selected these Black Friday deals (and excluded others)
 Rather than just reprint whatever deals the retailers are pushing, we start by going back to our (and your) favourite products of the last year. Then we look – everywhere – to see if they have genuinely good Black Friday deals.
 This often gives us a chance to re-recommend products we’ve rated highly, while wishing they weren’t so hair-raisingly pricey. “It’s so expensive,” wrote our best hair dryers tester Sarah Matthews about the Hershesons Great hair dryer . “The SmartSleep has a hefty price,” said Pete Wise of his favourite sunrise alarm for late-night reading. “Might feel like an investment too far,” mourned Lise Smith of the Dyson Airwrap Co-anda 2x multi-styler in her review . All are now discounted, and you’ll find their details below.
 We always make sure that the discounts are real and noteworthy, too. A crossed-out RRP isn’t enough. We research every product’s price history using tools such as the Camelizer (very efficient but Amazon-only) and PriceRunner (all retailers) to ensure these price cuts are rare enough to recommend. In markets that have received short shrift for misleading sales tactics , such as mattresses, we’ve been careful to feature significant deals only.
 The best early Black Friday deals on the Filter UK’s favourite products
 The best home deals 
 The gamechanging heated clothes airer
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Lakeland Dry:Soon Deluxe 3-tier heated airer with cover, from £183.73 (was £244.98) 
 £184.98 at Lakeland £183.73 at Amazon Heated clothes airers are a life-saver (for your laundry, at least) now that the rain and chill have returned, and Lakeland’s premium model beat all rivals in my test to find the best. It’s big and powerful enough to dry a small load in one go, especially with the fitted cover in place, and foldable enough to store in a cupboard or under the bed. It’s also pricey when not discounted, so this £60-off deal is very welcome – and it only costs around 8p an hour to run.
 The best unlit artificial Christmas tree
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Habitat 6ft mixed top upswept Christmas tree, £90 (was £120) 
 £90 at Argos Habitat’s gloriously lifelike and easy-to-assemble tree lost its best artificial Christmas tree crown to B&Q’s amazing pre-lit Fraser fir this year, but with the B&Q tree still costing £160 for a six-footer and the Habitat down to £90 for Black Friday, the canny option might be to plump for this one and add your own fairy lights , not least because they’re also included in the Argos Black Friday sale.
 Your favourite sunrise alarm clock
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Pete Wise/The Guardian Lumie sunrise alarm, from £37.49 (was £49) 
 £37.49 at Boots £39.20 at John Lewis The Lumie has been one of your favourite Filter recommendations ever since Pete Wise first tested it for his guide to the best sunrise alarm clocks . It’ll wake you up with kittens purring, birdsong or even goats bleating, or you can opt for gently brightening light – or a plain old buzzer. This price drop slightly eases the pain of dragging yourself out of bed in winter.
 Our favourite sunrise alarm clock
 View image in fullscreen Lumie Bodyclock Glow 150, from £84.79 (was £119) 
 £89.25 at Boots £84.79 at Amazon Our sunrise alarm tester Pete was even more keen on this Lumie model, which offers “medical-grade sunrise simulation” that proved the most realistic in Pete’s test: “like waking to daylight, or emerging into a clearing after walking through dense woodland”. It also packs a wide collection of wake-up sounds including a steam train, if that’s what floats your boat at 7am.
 The best cooling fan
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Caramel Quin/The Guardian AirCraft Lume fan, £129 (was £149) 
 £129 at AirCraft This summer’s ridiculous heat sent you mad … for electric fans. You couldn’t get enough of these things, wisely noting that they were cheaper than air conditioning and infinitely less hassle. Your favourite was the AirCraft Lume, winner of our test of the best fans and the one that did most to help our tester Caramel Quin – and the Filter’s deputy editor Monica Horridge – sleep in the heatwave . Snap it up at a bargain price while half the country has the heating on.
 Tough but chic suitcase
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Christian Hopewell/The Guardian Away the Large suitcase, £261 (was £348) 
 £261 at Away Pete Wise’s mission to find the best suitcase included a “drop test” that saw Pete hurl each case onto concrete from the top of a stepladder. Best survivor was this beautifully designed case from Away, which emerged “with just a few scuff marks” that Pete was able to remove using the special “eraser” sponge that comes included. “Superb finishing and toughness,” concluded Pete – now with 25% off.
 The best food, drink and kitchen deals 
 Manual espresso machine
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sasha Muller/The Guardian Sage Bambino Plus coffee machine, from £349 (was £399.00) 
 £349 at Coffee Friend £359.95 at John Lewis Named best manual machine for beginners in Sasha Muller’s guide to the best coffee machines , this beautiful brushed stainless steel model produces “fast, hassle-free coffee” and offers a “balance of coffee-brewing talent and beginner-friendly features can’t be beaten for the money. There’s no adjustable brew temperature, but this “neat little machine” is ideal for medium- to dark-roast coffee beans.
 Capsule espresso machine
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sasha Muller/The Guardian Lavazza Jolie Evo, from £45 (was £95) 
 £47.50 at Lavazza £45 at Amazon This compact capsule coffee machine would make a brilliant Christmas pressie for a fan of strong Italian espresso or black coffee, especially now that it’s around half price for Black Friday. Its design is a bit rough around the edges, but Sasha praised its “brash, nutty Italian espresso” and “consistently enjoyable coffee”. The Discover bundle of Sasha’s favourite A Modo Mio capsules is now discounted, too.
 Premium stand mixer
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Hiraki Sawa/The Guardian Kenwood Titanium Chef Baker, from £349.99 (was £529.99) 
 £399.99 at Kenwood £349.99 at Amazon “Serious home bakers who bake in big quantities and like high-tech appliances” will love this smooth, quiet and generously proportioned mixer, wrote Dale Berning Sawa in our guide to the best stand mixers , but it’s normally rather pricey. Amazon’s current deal is the cheapest online, but you’ll also find this mixer in Kenwood’s Black Friday sale , where dozens of premium kitchen items are treated to a discount.
 Classic Stanley insulated flask
 View image in fullscreen Stanley Classic thermal flask 1 l, from £29.33 (avg £36.91) 
 £39.20 at Stanley £29.33 at Amazon “Warming up from the inside and rehydrating with a hot, sweet drink is essential after a swim,” wrote Ella Foote in her wild swimming essentials guide. You can’t do better than Stanley’s leakproof design classic, which is widely available for about £50, even in the current sales. Amazon discounts it pretty regularly, but this Black Friday deal is still significantly less than the Stanley’s average Amazon price.
 Brilliant budget pizza oven
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Rachel Ogden/The Guardian ProCook outdoor pizza oven, £149 (was £249) 
 £149 at ProCook It’s nearly December and it gets dark at half four, but it’ll be spring again before you can say “April heatwave”, and it pays to think ahead. Even at full price, ProCook’s gas-powered outdoor oven was Rachel Ogden’s best budget option in her guide to the best pizza ovens . The pizzas could’ve risen better, but it’s “affordable, easily controllable and relatively simple to store [and] gets all the basics right”. Pineapple on mine, please.
 The most elegant toaster
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Rachel Ogden/The Guardian De’Longhi Ballerina Seta four-slice toaster, from £65 (was £74.99) 
 £65 at John Lewis £69 at De’Longhi This stunner from De’Longhi was already a fantastic value toaster that beat all rivals in Rachel Ogden’s guide to the best toasters . Shame it doesn’t have dual controls for the two pairs of slots, but “the tall toast it produced was some of the best I tried,” wrote Rachel, and it “performed brilliantly with frozen bread, turning out golden, evenly toasted slices.”
 Great value kettle
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Rachel Ogden/The Guardian Kenwood Ripple kettle, from £27.55 (was £39.99) 
 £29.99 at John Lewis £27.55 at Amazon “Kenwood’s Ripple kettle has a subtle design that belies its affordable price,” wrote Rachel Ogden in her guide to the best kettles . She admitted it feels a little flimsy compared with the premium kettles she’d been testing, but it packs in plenty of practical perks, including a 3kW element, a wide pouring spout to prevent drips and a clever plastic marker inside so you don’t need to watch the water window when filling.
 Carbon steel saucepan
 View image in fullscreen Misen 8in pre-seasoned carbon steel pan and lid, £86.25 (was £115) 
 £86.25 at Misen “Actual workhorses,” said chef and food writer Yotam Ottolenghi when suggesting Misen’s steel pans as brilliant Christmas presents. “They don’t scratch, the enamel doesn’t chip … They’ll outlast most of the things in my kitchen.” They’re popular with our Stateside counterparts, too. “Their prices reflect their long-lasting quality”, wrote the Filter’s US commissioning editor Karen Yuan. This 25% discount makes them an even wiser investment.
 Smashing little egg cooker
 View image in fullscreen Salter Aspen egg steamer, £10 (was £19) 
 £10 at Argos “I don’t know how I have cooked all these years without it,” admitted Filter reader and egg fan Amanda Nieurzyla-John in our roundup of everyday items that make your life better . Salter’s egg cooker can boil up to six eggs (soft, medium or hard) or poach two at a time, and at a sale price of £10 it’s a steal.
 Bean-to-cup coffee machine
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sasha Muller/The Guardian De’Longhi Magnifica Start, £299.99 (was £400) 
 £299.99 at Argos £299.99 at Amazon “Feed it with decent beans, and the Start will reward you with a tasty, balanced cup,” wrote our resident caffeine nut Sasha Muller, making this his top choice of best bean-to-cup coffee machine and declaring it the best-value option in the rundown. As Sasha presciently says, “keep an eye on the sales, and you can pick it up for £300 or so”.
 Our favourite leakproof mug
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Christian Hopewell/The Guardian Stanley AeroLight Transit insulated mug, from £21.25 (was £33) 
 £21.25 at Amazon Stanley’s beautiful, reusable 350ml mug keeps drinks hot all day and doesn’t spill a drop. Don’t take my word for it, take the word of our audacious travel mug tester Pete Wise, who “bounced on the trampette with it, shook it upside down, threw it over my head – and not a drop was spilled”. Many retailers have sold out, but Amazon has a few pastel-coloured options left, with light blue being cheapest.
 The best personal care deals 
 The multitalented toothbrush
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Alan Martin/The Guardian Spotlight Sonic Pro, £81 (was £99.99)

 £81 at Spotlight Oral Care with code FILTER10 Spotlight’s “early Black Friday” price of £90 is not a terrible discount (£10 off), but if you add the code FILTER10 at checkout you’ll get an extra 10% off, bringing it down to £81. Not at all bad for “a great all-rounder, with excellent features and a price that doesn’t verge on ridiculous,” which Alan Martin almost chose as his best overall electric toothbrush . (The crown was snatched at the last minute by the Laifen Wave Pro , which I’ll come to in a sec.)
 The best toothbrush we’ve tested
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Alan Martin/The Guardian Laifen Wave Pro, from about £79 (was £119.99) 
 €95 (about £79) at Laifen £87.99 at Amazon The Laifen arrived late in Alan’s test to find the best electric toothbrushes , and promptly toppled all comers by boasting “the most power and customisation of any brush I’ve tested” and leaving “my mouth feeling cleaner than ever”, despite dribbling a bit (the toothbrush, not Alan). Laifen’s store only has the pink version, and you’ll have to pay in euros. Amazon’s deal covers the silver and blue editions as well as pink.
 The deluxe hair dryer
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sarah Matthews/The Guardian Hershesons the Great hair dryer, £235 (was £295) 
 £235 at Hershesons Great by name, great by nature, great big price tag. The magnificent Hershesons dryer was Sarah Matthews’ top overall pick in best hair dryers , because it “perfects the basics and irons out any common niggles” and left her hair “soft and healthy-looking”. At well over £200, it’s still pretty pricey, but you can’t do much better if you’re looking for an investment hair dryer.
 The squishy rabbit vibrator
 View image in fullscreen Hera Flex, £89 (was £99) 
 £89 at Je Joue It’s not a massive discount, but this vibrator has been so popular with Filter readers that we don’t doubt you’ll welcome the savings. Alix Fox declared Je Joue’s “thoughtfully re-engineered rabbit reboot” to be “as flexible as a yoga master” in her guide to the best vibrators , saying it’s rather squishy but versatile enough to suit many different anatomical configurations.
 The best budget LED mask
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sarah Matthews/The Guardian Silk’n Facial LED face mask 100, from £71.99 (was £160) 
 £71.99 at Boots with code EBSAVE10 £78.06 at Lookfantastic with code EXTRA Already your best bet to “try light therapy without remortgaging the house”, writes Sarah Matthews in her guide to the best LED face masks , this comfortable silicone mask lacks the premium features of its more expensive counterparts (no timer or near-infrared, for instance), but left Sarah’s face “feeling completely comfortable, with a glowier finish than usual”. Use the discount codes to get the best prices.
 The customisable LED mask
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Sarah Matthews/The Guardian CurrentBody Series 3, £399.99 (was £499.99) 
 £399.99 at Currentbody Sarah’s best-rated LED mask overall, which also earned a five-star review , gets a welcome £100 discount for Black Friday. “The redness in my cheeks had faded, my chin appeared to clear quickly after a particularly brutal hormonal breakout, and the rest of my skin looked glowier and healthier than usual after my six weeks of testing,” she wrote of this fully customisable model.
 The best sleep deals 
 Our favourite bed in a box
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Otty Original Hybrid double mattress, £559.99 (was £624.99) 
 £559.99 at Otty The best mattress I’ve ever tested , Otty’s bed-in-a-box mattress dazzled me (to sleep) with its outstanding balance of support, cushioning and breathability. It’s already an excellent buy, costing less than half the price of the similarly comfy Simba Hybrid Pro (more on that in a moment), and this £65-off Black Friday deal makes it even easier to recommend.
 The best mattress for couples
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Simba Hybrid Pro double mattress , £909.30 (was £1,299) 
 £909.30 at Simba Simba’s sumptuous mattress is a fine choice for side sleepers who need a little extra cushioning, and it helped me sleep by absorbing the tossing and turning of my restless husband. It gets a sizeable 33% discount for Black Friday – as does everything in Simba’s range of premium sleep products, which also includes my favourite mattress topper (the Simba Hybrid topper , down from £349 to £296.65 for a double) and one of my best-testing duvets (the Simba Hybrid 10.5-tog duvet , down from £199 to £149.25 for a double).
 The best firm mattress
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Origin Hybrid Pro double mattress , £599 (was £795) 
 £599 at Origin This huge mattress may be just what you’re after if you crave a firmer bed, especially if you’re a large sleeper or tend to sleep on your back. It has a reassuringly orthopaedic feel and a lovely silky surface that feels cooling under your body, and it’s great value for such a robust mattress. At 31cm deep, it needs an extra-deep fitted sheet, though (these bamboo sheets from Panda would work, and they’re reduced too).
 Premium mattress topper
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Simba Hybrid double mattress topper , £296.65 (was £349) 
 £296.65 at Simba I named the luxurious Hybrid topper my favourite overall in our guide to the best mattress toppers , saying it’s ideal for “anyone who loves a cosy but supportive sleeping surface and doesn’t want to fork out for an entire hybrid mattress”. It’s still pricey for a topper, but with layers of foam and springs and a removable cover, it’s more sophisticated than many entire beds.
 The best pregnancy pillow
 View image in fullscreen Bbhugme pregnancy pillow, £127.20 (was £159) 
 £127.20 at John Lewis £127.20 at Mamas and Papas “A great all-rounder,” wrote Victoria Turk, naming the microbead-pilled Bbhugme as best overall in her test to find the best pregnancy pillows . “I can see it being useful at all stages of pregnancy, as support needs shift, and after birth as a nursing bolster.” The pillow impressed her with its comfy flexibility and light weight but she wished it weren’t so pricey, so this £31 discount will be very welcome if you’re expecting.
 Cooling mattress topper
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jane Hoskyn/The Guardian Panda double mattress topper , £118.96 (was £139.95) 
 £118.96 at Panda The Panda was your favourite from our best mattress toppers rundown, and its ability to soothe my pain and help me sleep earned it a five-star review . It’s an excellent buy even at full price, adding a 5cm layer of cushioning, support and temperature control to your bed. This 15%-off deal is one of Panda’s more modest Black Friday cuts; you get 20% off its Hybrid Bamboo Pillow and a full 30% off its mattresses .
 Our favourite pillow
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Edward Munn/The Guardian Otty Deluxe Pure bamboo memory foam pillow, £54.99 (was £69.99) 
 £54.99 at Otty Otty is proving hard to dislodge from the top of our sleep roundups, taking the number one spot in best pillows as well as best mattresses . “The Deluxe Pure manages to strike a happy middle ground” between firm and cushioned, wrote our pillow tester Edward Munn, who said it never felt hot or needed plumping up and is “a great choice for those who move around between different sleeping positions.”
 The best fitness deals 
 The best budget treadmill
 View image in fullscreen JTX Slimline, £429 (was £549) 
 £429 at JTX with code FILTER50 At a usual price of £549, this “best budget” pick from our guide to the best treadmills will seriously stretch your pocket money (indoor running doesn’t come cheap), but the JTX sale brings it down to a more reasonable £479 – and a Filter-exclusive code knocks another £50 off, right up until the end of December. Our tester Leon Poultney loved the Slimline’s compact size and foldability, hailing it as a great choice if you lack the space for a full-size treadmill, but warned that it’s not sturdy enough for intense workouts.
 Best gym-quality treadmill
 View image in fullscreen JTX Sprint-9 Pro, £1,449 (was £1,699) 
 £1,449 at JTX with code FILTER50 This absolute beast is the one to go for if you want to continue your intense runs indoors all winter. “Built to last, comes with a generous warranty and provides a similar experience to what you might find in your local gym,” wrote Leon when choosing it as his best gym-quality pick in best treadmills , adding that it has 36 preinstalled workout programmes and a “serious incline” to boost your strength and power.
 The best running shoes
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Jill Mead/The Guardian Saucony Endorphin Azura, from £95.90 (was from £109.99) 
 Men’s 
 £95.90 at Running Point £111.89 at Cotswold Outdoor Women’s 
 £98 at John Lewis The best running shoes for you depends on many things including your taste and running gait, but Kieran Alger has put hundreds of pairs to the test, and he found these Sauconys hard to beat as neutral all-rounders. “They’re high-energy, well-cushioned, nicely balanced” shoes that “feel instantly at home and natural on the foot,” he wrote, calling them “an ideal pick for marathon training”. They’re widely available online, but these are the best early Black Friday deals we could find with a decent range of sizes.
 The best fashion deals 
 Cashmere bandana
 View image in fullscreen Rise & Fall cashmere micro-bandana, £44 (was £55) 
 £44 at Rise & Fall One of Jess Cartner-Morley’s style essentials for autumn 2026, this cute cashmere bandana has teardrop-point ends making it easy to knot with minimal bulk. Jess is a big fan of British brand Rise & Fall, which buys direct from the manufacturers of the finest materials, including fine cashmere and organic cotton, and sells them without the retail mark-up. Now an even better buy, and a lovely gift idea.
 Boxy tweed jacket
 View image in fullscreen Mango tweed jacket with notched lapel collar, £62.99 (was £89.99) 
 £62.99 at Mango “Jeans and a jacket is the normcore power suit,” wrote Jess Cartner-Morley back in the hazy days of summer, when putting on a Chanel-like “jazzy boucle tweed with shiny buttons” was strictly for cold-bloods and masochists. Now that tweed jacket and shiny button season is in full swing, this ecru number from Mango fits the bill (and the weather) perfectly. And it’s 30% off for Black Friday.
 Comfy walking sandals
 View image in fullscreen FitFlop Neo-D-Hyker, from £55 (was £95) 
 From £55 at Fitflop The beige Neo-D-Hykers so beloved by Sian Lewis in best walking sandals for women are now sold out, but these near-identical pairs come in a range of sizes and colours including black and apricot, with cappuccino being cheapest. “So cloud-like that you’ll forget you’re wearing them, the Neo-D-Hykers top my list of walking sandals for comfort,” wrote Sian. Buy now, and your toes will thank you come summer.
 For more, read our guide to the best sustainable Black Friday deals 
 View image in fullscreen Black Friday is a confusing time to shop, with dodgy discounts on sub-par products being advertised everywhere you look. But it can also be a great opportunity to save money if you shop wisely. To help you navigate the noise, we pore over thousands of deals and only recommend genuinely good savings on the products we love, as well as offering buying advice to help you stay savvy.
